newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - October 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - October 7.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi. Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006 E-mail:biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
Indian Express
FORMER FINANCE MINISTER IN CONGRESS WORKING COMMITTEE

Former finance minister Manmohan Singh has been inducted into the elite Congress Working Committee (CWC). Congress party's president, Sitaram Kesri, after announcing Singh's entry into CWC, warned against any bid by the ruling United Front (UF) government to split the Congress party. Kesri said any efforts by UF to break the Congress would result in its being toppled, as its survival depended on Congress support. Singh's inclusion in CWC fuelled speculation that Kesri was trying to sideline former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao, currently facing criminal charges in the court, to refurbish the party's image.
The Economic Times
INDIAN CORPORATES LAUNCH INDIA CLUB

Indian corporates, put under competitive pressure by economic reforms, have decided to regroup themselves to put pressure on the government against favouring foreign multinationals. The group, to be called India Club, plans to caution the government on the adverse implications of its economic policies serving multinational corporations' interests.
HIGHER CAPITAL GOOD IMPORTS FORETELL GROWTH

Companies have sought higher capital goods import, under the export promotion of capital goods (EPCG) scheme, in the first quarter of fiscal 1996/97 (April-March) compared to 1995/96. The directorate-general of foreign trade, during the period, issued licence for import of capital goods worth 36.1 billion rupees providing for an export obligation of about 210 billion rupees.
INSTITUTIONAL SANCTIONS DROP 20 PCT

Investment sanctions by financial institutions (FI) witnessed a sharp dip in the first half of the current financial year, 1996/97 (April-March). Estimates show a minimum 20 percent slowdown in total sanction figures for the half-year. According to available statistics, the investment proposals slowed down dramatically, whereas new applications were hardly coming in. Approvals made by FIs during April-July 1996 were down 22 percent to 129.29 billion rupees from 165.5 billion rupees in the same period last year.
OMAN SCRAPS $10 BLN PIPELINE PROJECT

Oman has scrapped the $10-billion gas pipeline project with India due to financial and technological problems. This is despite the fact that Oman had already spent $70 million on feasibility studies. The project, if completed, would have initially exported one billion cubic feet of Omani gas to India daily from 1999.
INDUSTRY BODY FOR 20 PCT INSTITUTIONAL STAKE IN FIRMS

The Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) has demanded a 20 percent ceiling on financial institutions' (FI) holdings in private sector companies. CII further suggested that present FI holdings in excess of 20 percent should be divested gradually without destabilising the securities market. The CII note on the draft takeover code also said the threshold limit for an obligatory offer to other shareholders should be 25 percent, instead of the currently proposed limit of 10 percent.
Financial Express
FOREIGN STAKE IN DOMESTIC AIRLINES MAY NOT BE ALLOWED

The federal government plans to ask foreign airlines holding equity in Indian carriers, to divest their stake under a new aviation policy scheduled to be announced in November. This was announced by the Civil Aviation Minister. The minister ruled out the chances of Tatas-Singapore Airlines project entering the country. Under the new policy, no foreign participation would be allowed in domestic sector. The policy may immediately affect Gulf Air and Kuwait Airways who hold 20 percent stake each in Jet Airways.
PUBLIC SECTOR BANKS TO COME UNDER COMPANIES ACT

In a sweeping stand to bring about uniformity among the public sector banks, the Finance Ministry plans to abolish the State Bank of India Act 1995 and the Banking Regulation Act 1970. The ministry plans to bring all banks under the Companies Act. The ministry is also considering an alternative plan to merge theses Acts to create a common law for the industry.
INFLATION SHOOTS UP TO 6.52 PCT

Continuing its rising trend for the seventh successive week, annual rate of inflation gained 0.27 percentage points to touch a 38-week high of 6.52 percent for week ended September 21. Fuelled largely by an increase in petroleum prices, inflation swelled by over 1.4 percentage points in the last three months. The index for fuel, power, light and lubricants rose by 1.8 percent to 333 from 324.3 in the last week due to higher prices of coking coal (25 percent) and non-coking coal (nine percent). Inflation was placed at 8.9 percent during the corresponding period of the previous year.
ITALIAN CAR MAJOR PLANS PALIO CAR PROJECT IN COUNTRY

Italian automobile giant Fiat Spa plans to set up a greenfield project in India to make its Palio cars. Premier Automobiles Ltd (PAL) is likely to be Fiat's partner for the project. However, a final decision on the matter is still awaited. Fiat has a technical collaboration with PAL for the manufacture of the Uno car at Premier's manufacturing facility in Kurla, a suburb of Bombay..
Business Standard
FISCAL DEFICIT TARGET UNDER PRESSURE

The fiscal deficit target for the current financial year has come under pressure due to uncertainty regarding revenue and divestment receipts. The pressure on government to hike defence expenditure has further worsened the situation. The divestment programme of the government for raising 50 billion rupees is set to take off in January. Even though this may partially salvage the situation, the revenue department is worried that the current slowdown in economy could affect government revenues. The government has targetted the fiscal deficit for the year at 5.0 percent of gross domestic product.
CORE SECTOR INVESTMENT MAY RISE TO $30 BLN

India's infrastructure investment may rise from current $17 billion a year to about $30 billion by the year 2000, says an official paper. It says the total infrastructure investment requirements over the next five year will be $115 billion to $130 billion. This may rise to $215 billion in the next five years. The paper expects about 15 percent of total capital requirements for infrastructure to be externally financed. These projections would be discussed at the coming United Nations' Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific (ESCAP) ministerial conference on infrastructure to be held in Delhi from October 23 to 30.
